You are optimizing a palladium-catalysed Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling run in flow, which forms a new carbon-carbon bond between an aryl halide and an organoboron partner; the active catalyst is a palladium centre bound to a phosphine ligand.

Your objective is to MAXIMIZE the reaction yield — the percentage of the limiting substrate converted to the desired coupled product.

You control the following parameters (each with its physical role and allowed range):

  - res_time — residence time (range [60, 600] s): how long reagents spend in the reactor — longer allows more conversion but also more catalyst decomposition and side-reactions
  - temperature — reactor temperature (range [30, 110] deg C): raises the reaction rate but can degrade the catalyst or promote side-pathways
  - catalyst_loading — catalyst loading (range [0.498, 2.515] mol%): how much palladium catalyst is used relative to substrate — more speeds the reaction but adds cost and can favour decomposition

turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the data

**Ligand choice.** Sorting by yield, L3 dominates the top of the table (98.7, 91.3, 83.9, 83.1, 80.2, 78.1…), and it performs well across *two distinct regimes* (long time/low loading and short time/high loading), which indicates a genuinely robust, active catalyst rather than a lucky single point. L6 and L0 are the runners-up (85.4, 81.3, 69.6) but never exceed ~85%. L5 is clearly the worst (single-digit yields even at 110 °C). So **L3**.

**Temperature.** Every high yield in the dataset is at 110 °C; at 30–70 °C yields collapse to 0.6–30% for all ligands. The Ar–X oxidative addition/transmetalation barrier evidently dominates over catalyst decomposition here, so push temperature to the **maximum, 110 °C**.

**Catalyst loading.** At 110 °C, high loading (~2.5 mol%) gives the best short-residence results for every ligand (L3 98.7, L6 85.4, L2 62.8). With L3 at 1.1–1.27 mol% you need the full 600 s and still only reach 72–91%. More Pd → faster turnover, letting you finish before catalyst death. So use loading near the top: **~2.51 mol%**.

**Residence time.** This is the one non-monotonic knob. With L3 at 2.508 mol%: 189 s → 98.7%, 200 s → 83.9%; L6 at 2.5 mol% shows the same decline past ~155–175 s (85.4 → 81.3 → 68.6 → 75). At 110 °C with high Pd, the reaction is essentially complete in ~2–3 min, and extra time only lets the Pd–phosphine catalyst decompose (Pd black) and drives protodeboronation/dehalogenation side pathways. So sit right in that ~180–195 s window rather than going longer.

**Proposed optimum:** L3 at 110 °C, ~2.51 mol% Pd, residence time ~188 s — the peak of the observed L3 response surface, nudged marginally toward slightly higher loading (faster completion, so the conversion plateau is reached a bit earlier and less time is spent in the decomposition-dominated regime).

**Final: ligand=L3, res_time=188, temperature=110, catalyst_loading=2.515**
